subject: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Mendes <alicia.mendes@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Hi Alicia — great to meet today. Quick recap from our side and a path forward on procurement so we don’t lose momentum:

Call notes (short):
- Brightbridge is interested in a 3-month pilot (1-2 seats, test workloads).
- Procurement prefers PO for production; procurement team requires vendor to be registered in their marketplace before issuing a PO.
- Procurement said corporate card is acceptable for pilot purchases under $15k.

Open questions we flagged:
- How long is procurement’s marketplace listing approval (you mentioned ~3–4 weeks)?
- Will Finance accept a Redwood W-9 and vendor portal invite to speed onboarding?

Action items I’ll start:
1) Attach SOW draft and our W-9 for procurement (attached: SOW-draft-Brightbridge-Redwood.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf).
2) I’ll send a vendor portal invite if you confirm the marketplace URL and contact.
3) If marketplace listing will block the PO, we can propose a card-based pilot (<= $15k) while listing completes — need your confirmation.

Would you prefer we (a) pursue marketplace listing now and wait for PO, or (b) sign a small-card pilot to prove value and convert to PO? If (b) we can offer a short credit for the pilot while you complete onboarding — happy to discuss details.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Sean and Marissa for the vendor-portal steps.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: SOW-draft-Brightbridge-Redwood.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf
From: Alicia Mendes <alicia.mendes@brightbridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@brightbridge.com>, procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Thanks, Rachel — appreciate the clear notes. Confirming what I mentioned on the call: our procurement team requires vendors to be registered in our vendor marketplace before they will issue a PO. The marketplace review is mostly administrative but can take 3–4 weeks depending on our vendor team backlog.

Two practical options for us:
1) Marketplace -> PO: Marketplace registration first, then procurement issues a Net-30 PO for production-level contracts.
2) Card-first pilot: Procurement allows a card payment for pilots under $15k so we can start immediately. If the pilot proves out, we move to PO for scale.

Procurement needs the W-9 and the vendor portal invite (or the marketplace registration link). I’ve cc’d Tom from procurement to speed the vendor question.

If we go card for the pilot, I’ll need a simple invoice and a credit card-friendly payment method (we use Concur). If you could confirm the pilot price estimate, I can review with Tom and finance and get back by end of week.

Alicia
Head of Data Platforms | Brightbridge Analytics
alicia.mendes@brightbridge.com | +1 (212) 555-0190
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Team — forwarding Alicia’s reply. Key constraints: marketplace listing required for PO (3–4 weeks), card OK for pilot <= $15k. Procurement (Tom) needs W-9 + vendor invite.

Options I recommend (priority order):
- Option A (fastest to start): Card-backed pilot for immediate start (<= $15k). We invoice and they pay via Concur.
- Option B (longer-term): Start marketplace registration today and plan for PO: gather docs (W-9, SOW, MSA).

Two asks for you:
- Sean: Can you prepare a vendor portal invite + marketplace registration checklist so Alicia can forward to Tom?
- Ben: Would leadership approve a small pilot credit (we discussed $5k) to overcome the friction and accelerate an eventual larger PO? If yes, I’ll offer that to Alicia for the pilot.

I’ve attached the SOW and W-9 in case procurement needs copies again. I’ll wait for Sean’s portal invite and Ben’s decision before responding to Alicia with next steps.

Thanks,
Rachel
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Got it — I’ll assemble the vendor portal invite and marketplace checklist this morning. Will include:
- Redwood company details + W-9 (we already have the W-9 attached)
- Sample invoice template for Concur/card processing
- Point of contact for marketplace compliance items

If leadership can confirm a pilot credit, we should offer it as an incentive to go card-first and shorten time to value. Ben — any objection to $5k credit for a short pilot? I’ll include the credit in the SOW amendment if approved.

Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Approved — offer a $5k pilot credit and prioritize marketplace listing support.

Guidance:
- Credit applied to pilot invoice; pilot capped at $15k card charge.
- We’ll expedite a simplified MSA for a pilot (legal to prepare a short-form addendum). Rachel — you can promise the credit to Alicia and request their procurement team start marketplace onboarding immediately.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Mendes <alicia.mendes@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@brightbridge.com>, procurement@brightbridge.com, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement path clarity — PO vs card and vendor onboarding next steps

Alicia — thanks for the quick reply. Confirming next steps from Redwood: 

1) We’ll support marketplace registration immediately — Sean will send the vendor portal invite + checklist to you and Tom within the hour.
2) To avoid delay, we can start a card-pay pilot (<= $15k). We’ll apply a $5k pilot credit as a one-time adjustment to the pilot invoice; total customer card charge will be capped at $10k after credit (example pricing attached in SOW).
3) Legal will prepare a short-form pilot addendum / MSA that can be signed quickly; we’ll send a DocuSign link (see related link).

Please confirm which path you prefer (Marketplace -> PO or Card pilot + marketplace in parallel). If card pilot, please share the Concur invoice contact and preferred billing address so we can produce an invoice immediately.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
